models_evaluated: deep learning optic disc segmentation models

links.outcome: Glaucoma classification and optic disc segmentation performance of public-trained vs local real-world-data-trained models on local test data
links.effect: Public models dropped 8.0% (OD segmentation, to 85.6%) and 18.4% (glaucoma classification, to 76.6%) on RWD; RWD-trained models outperformed public models on RWD by 2.0% and 9.5%.
links.quote: RWD models outperformed public models on RWD test sets by 2.0% and 9.5%, respectively, in OD segmentation and glaucoma classification tasks.

links.outcome: Performance of models trained on local real-world data versus public data when tested on local data
links.effect: RWD-trained models outperformed public-trained models on RWD test sets by 2.0% (OD segmentation) and 9.5% (glaucoma classification).
links.quote: RWD models outperformed public models on RWD test sets by 2.0% and 9.5%, respectively, in OD segmentation and glaucoma classification tasks.

screen.reason: Empirical study testing the generalizability of deep learning ophthalmic models on real-world clinical dataset vs public training datasets (external validation/domain transfer evaluation).
